You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: Spinner]

Roland’s spinner has three sectors of different colors, orange, purple, and green. Roland spins the pointer 1000 times. The chart below shows how many times the pointer stops on each section.

| Color | Times Stopped |
| :--- | :---: |
| Orange | 510 |
| Purple | 243 |
| Green | 247 |

Draw lines on the spinner above to make the three sectors the approximate size you would expect them to be. Label them orange, purple, and green.

Figure, described in words:
A circular spinner with a central circular hub and an arrow pointer angled upward and to the right. Around the circumference of the circle is an outer rim with 8 equally spaced tick marks, dividing the circle into 8 equal arcs of 45° each (at 12 o'clock, 1:30, 3 o'clock, 4:30, 6 o'clock, 7:30, 9 o'clock, and 10:30). The interior of the circle is blank.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Draw three lines from the center to the circumference to make sectors of about 184° for orange, 87° for purple, and 89° for green. Using the tick marks, these can be approximated as 180°, 90°, and 90°: make the orange sector half the circle and the purple and green sectors each one quarter. Label each sector.
